title: Common lower-truncation coproduct comparison for derived direct image
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let $I$ be a set and $E_i$ a family in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category]. Let $S\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ with maps $\iota_i:E_i\to S$ which exhibit an ambient coproduct. Write $F_q=H^q\circ Rf_*$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image]. For every pair of integers $a,q$, the canonical map $\bigoplus_i F_q(\tau_{\ge a}E_i)\to F_q(\tau_{\ge a}S)$ whose restriction to the $i$th summand is $F_q(\tau_{\ge a}\iota_i)$ is an isomorphism. Here $\tau_{\ge a}$ is canonical lower truncation for the standard cohomological t-structure.

source.place: Tag 08DZ, bounded-below spectral-sequence paragraph, with Tag 015J

proof.text: Construct coproduct projections π_i:S→E_i from hc. For H=H^q Rf_* τ≥a, additivity gives H(ι_j)H(π_i)=δ_ij. These projections prove injectivity of the direct-sum comparison in modules; prove it sectionwise for presheaves, and transfer it through exact module sheafification to a monomorphism of module sheaves. No quasi-coherence or boundedness is needed for this step.

On every affine open U, use the finite-support theorem to obtain a preimage of every target section in the algebraic direct sum. Map that finite-support element into sections of the sheaf coproduct using the section maps of its coprojections. DirectSum.linearMap_ext and functoriality identify the composite with the supplied surjective map. Thus evaluation of the comparison is epi; it is mono by preservation of monomorphisms by evaluation, hence an isomorphism.
Affine opens form a basis. Apply TopCat.Sheaf.isIso_iff_isIso_basis to the underlying abelian sheaf morphism and reflect the resulting isomorphism through SheafOfModules.toSheaf.

proof_origin.place: Split the affine-section surjectivity component; prove injectivity using coproduct projections, then combine and use the affine basis criterion.
